content.user_title: Edit Images with Intent-Based RunComfy Routing
content.value_statement: Different image edits require different models and input formats. This skill selects a RunComfy route and prepares model-specific prompts and CLI requests.
actual_capabilities: Route requests to Nano Banana Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, Flux Kontext Pro, or Z-Image Turbo Inpaint based on intent.
Prepare Nano Banana requests with 1 to 20 input image URLs and consistent aspect ratio and resolution settings.
Prepare multilingual text replacement and numbered reference-image composition requests for GPT Image 2 Edit.
Prepare single-reference local edits with preservation instructions for Flux Kontext Pro.
Configure grayscale-mask inpainting with strength and control settings for region removal or replacement.
Provide RunComfy CLI examples, output-directory options, and documented exit-code explanations.
limitations: Requires the external RunComfy CLI, an authenticated account, and network access; this skill does not implement image editing locally.
Input images and masks require server-accessible URLs; remote processing is unsuitable for assets without permission for external sharing.
Each call uses one model; reference counts, sizes, and mask requirements vary by route.
The supplied file contains instructions, not tested results or CLI source; model availability, security protections, and output quality are not independently verified.

use_cases.title: Standardize Product Image Backgrounds
use_cases.description: Prepare consistent background edits for a product series while specifying preserved subjects, aspect ratio, and resolution.

use_cases.title: Localize Text in Campaign Images
use_cases.description: Request exact headline replacements in another language while preserving the photograph, brand mark, and layout.

use_cases.title: Retouch Selected Photo Regions
use_cases.description: Prepare masked removal or replacement requests with explicit preservation boundaries and suitable strength settings.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Replace a Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit the image at [image URL]. Replace only the background with light gray studio paper. Preserve the subject, pose, and clothing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A single image with a simple background change.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Edit a Product Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit for [image URLs]. Apply a consistent white background and preserve each product. Set aspect ratio 1:1 and resolution 1K.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product series with 1 to 20 source images.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Localize an Image Headline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 Edit on [poster URL]. Replace only the headline with "[exact text]" using [script]. Preserve the photograph, logo, and layout.
prompt_templates.scenario: A campaign image requiring precise translated text.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Configure Masked Replacement
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Z-Image Turbo Inpaint with [image URL] and [mask URL]. Replace the white-masked region with [replacement]. Preserve unmasked details. Set strength [value].
prompt_templates.scenario: A prepared grayscale mask controlling a regional replacement.

output_examples.input: Choose a route for three product images that need matching white backgrounds.
output: Illustrative request plan: Nano Banana Edit with three source image URLs.
Preservation: keep product shapes, labels, and colors unchanged.
Execution requires authenticated RunComfy access; this example does not include a generated image.

output_examples.input: Choose a route to remove cables from a street photograph using a prepared grayscale mask.
output: Illustrative request plan: Z-Image Turbo Inpaint with the source image and mask URLs.
Mask: white selects cables for editing; black preserves surrounding areas.
Initial settings: strength 0.5 and control scale 0.8, following the documented removal example.
Preservation: retain rooflines and the sky gradient; inspect the generated result for artifacts.

best_practices: State what must remain unchanged before describing the edit, and split complex changes into smaller passes.
Verify permission for remote processing, protect credentials, and use approved image URLs before running the CLI.
Match the route to reference counts and mask availability; inspect generated images for text errors and unintended changes.
anti_patterns: Sending confidential images or credentials through unapproved public URLs or placing tokens inside prompts.
Using a single-reference route for multiple images or requesting inpainting without a grayscale mask.
Combining many unrelated changes in one request and assuming subject identity or text accuracy is guaranteed.

faq.question: What must be installed before running an edit?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI and authenticate with a RunComfy account. The skill documents login and an environment-token option for CI.

faq.question: How does the skill choose a model?
faq.answer: It maps the requested edit to four documented routes. Nano Banana Edit is the default when no specialized intent is identified.

faq.question: How many reference images can I provide?
faq.answer: The guide lists up to 20 inputs for Nano Banana and 10 for GPT Image 2 Edit. Flux Kontext accepts one reference.

faq.question: Do all edits require a mask?
faq.answer: No. The Z-Image Turbo Inpaint route requires a grayscale mask. White marks areas to edit; black marks areas to preserve.

faq.question: Are images processed on my computer?
faq.answer: No. The documented CLI workflow sends requests to RunComfy, where servers fetch input URLs. Generated outputs are downloaded to the selected directory.

faq.question: Are the example results guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. The examples illustrate request plans, not tested outputs. Quality, text accuracy, service availability, and subject preservation depend on the selected model.
